kind: A diagnostic in floats at full size, never a path: the full-size Transformer of the rate pilot with the stack's kind of pool in place of its LayerNorms, and with an output layer of its own, 24,000 updates at 3e-4, one seed each.
why: After 24,000 updates at 3e-4 the float stand-in of the stack is 0.0290 behind the Transformer (full_size_spikes_late.json), and the stack's kind of unit costs the Transformer 0.0077 of that (full_size_units_in_floats.json, under the mark of 0.009), so about 0.021 of the layout's distance lies elsewhere. That record's reading walks the rest of the layout next: the pool in place of a norm and the output's own weights. v15's walk priced both at 9,000 updates and a rate of 0.001 (docs/STREAM_FORM.md): the output's own weights 0.0065, and the fine pool 0.0118, which was the membranes' saturation at that rate (at 3e-4 the pool was ahead of LayerNorm). Neither has been priced late, at the rate where the full-size pair is compared on the way, or with the pool as a float control of the Transformer itself.

arms.fs-tf3-pool: --transformer-norm pool (35c4a97): every LayerNorm of the Transformer, two in each block and one before the output, becomes a pool that divides the stream by its mean absolute activity and a learned rest, with a gain per channel and no centring, as a stack's inhibitory pool raises every threshold with the stream's activity; 34,740,247 parameters, the LayerNorms' biases gone (23 norms of 512 channels lose 511 parameters each)
arms.fs-tf3-own: --untied-output: the output layer has weights of its own in place of the embedding's, as the stack's output synapses have; 34,883,072 parameters (131,072 more)

base: fs-tf3 of full_size_rate_pilot (1.30572): the full-size Transformer with LayerNorms and tied output weights, the same recipe, seed and measure; beside it fs-tf3-relu (1.31341), fs-float3 (1.33471) and fs-st3 (1.34164).
runs: sched/bin/full.sh transformer NAME FLAG: 24,000 updates of 8 windows of 512 bytes, peak rate 3e-4, warmup 1,000, cosine over the run, seed 20001, on the code copy of 35c4a97, on GPU 0 at priority 37, after the sleep and phase screens' runs.
measure: As full_size_units_in_floats.json: averaged weights on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes in windows of 496 bytes of history before 16 scored, bits of every piece kept; each arm paired with fs-tf3 (experiments/compare_stream_scores.py) and split by context (experiments/gap_by_piece.py, near 496, far 8,192).
reading: One seed: these readings direct the next work and are not findings about the parts. The price of each part is the arm minus fs-tf3, read against what the unit leaves of the layout's distance, 0.0213 (0.0290 minus 0.0077). (1) A part whose price is at least half of that, 0.0107, is the larger part of what remains, and the next spiking work goes to it: for the pool, a normalization that centres as well as divides (a pool of inhibitory cells that subtracts the stream's mean activity before the threshold divides by it); for the output, an output layer that shares the input's synapses on the full-size stack (it failed on the test bed, shunt_tied/preregistered.json, so only at full size). (2) A part whose price is below a quarter, 0.0053, is a small part. (3) If both are small, the remaining distance lies in what neither diagnostic touched, the reads' layout and the stream's pulse budget, and the next diagnostic walks those. Reported either way: each price with its paired interval and its part on new contexts.
seen_before_recording: full_size_units_in_floats.json with its result; v15's walk at 9,000 updates (docs/STREAM_FORM.md); the arms' code built and tested (35c4a97: the pool's tests; the untied output's from before), and a pool-norm Transformer trained two updates on the laptop's CPU. No arm of this record has trained.
